I have resolved the issue where deferred fields were incorrect when following nested prefetches back to the parent object.

### Cause
When evaluating nested prefetch lookups (e.g. `User.objects.only("email").prefetch_related(Prefetch("profile", queryset=Profile.objects.prefetch_related(Prefetch("user", queryset=User.objects.only("kind")))))`), evaluating the inner `Profile` queryset triggered its nested prefetches first, populating `Profile.user` with the inner `User` instance (where `kind` was fetched and `email` was deferred).

However, during `get_prefetch_queryset` on `ReverseOneToOneDescriptor` (and similarly `ForwardManyToOneDescriptor` and `ForeignRelatedObjectsDescriptor`), Django manually set reverse relation caches on the prefetched objects. This unconditionally overwrote `Profile.user` cache with the outer `User` instance (where `email` was loaded and `kind` was deferred), discarding the freshly prefetched `User` object and causing subsequent attribute accesses to execute extra database queries.

### Solution
In [`django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-lrb8_kxo/django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py#L145-L149), check whether the reverse relationship is already cached on `rel_obj` (`if not ...is_cached(rel_obj):`) before populating the reverse relation cache in `get_prefetch_queryset` methods.
